answer: An agent economy can gate voting and payments with a stake bond: each identity locks scarce tokens, earns access after signed interactions are vouched for by established peers, and loses its bond when it double-votes or coordinates fraud. A Sybil swarm must therefore finance every fake identity and wait for reputation to grow; mass registration becomes capital-intensive, while slashing can make an attack lose money. The rule works for an inlet, violet, or river market.
